prs.title: fix: reset local expect state between retries for `expect.assertions/hasAssertions`
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- extracted from https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11892

Previously, the test's own `expect` (`({ expect }) => ...`) kept its assertion count across retries and repeats, so `expect.assertions(n)` failed on every attempt after the first:

```ts
let attempt = 0
test('retry', { retry: 1 }, ({ expect }) => {
  attempt++
  expect.assertions(1)
  expect(attempt).toBe(2)
})
// Error: expected number of assertions to be 1, but got 2
```

This PR resets the local `expect` state before each attempt, as was already done for the global `expect`.

prs.title: fix(mocker): keep re-exports of hoisted imports
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Fixes #11866

`hoistMocks` replaces a static import with a dynamic import, so `export { a }` of an imported binding pointed to a binding that no longer exists. The value was `undefined` with the module runner, and browser mode failed with `SyntaxError: Export 'a' is not defined in module`. The transform now declares `const a = __vi_import_0__.a` after the hoisted import.

The re-export is a copy of the value, not a live binding. A static `export { a } from './a'` would keep the live binding, but it loads the module before the hoisted `vi.mock` runs.

prs.title: fix(cache): watch cached files outside the root
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Vite adds a file outside the root to the watcher when it transforms the file. A cache hit skips the transform, so a warm `vitest --watch` did not rerun tests when that file changed.

Fixes #11584

prs.title: feat(cache): add fs module cache env variables
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Adds `VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE` and `VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH`. The config and the CLI take priority over them.

Fixes #11847

prs.title: fix(cache): treat a removed cache file as a miss
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
A cache file that another process removes between the check and the read is now a cache miss. Every cold run takes this path, so the existing tests cover it.

The worker can still fail if the file is removed after the server returns its path. Refs #11843
